pairs.question: Quid vos, Brute et Attice? numquid tandem novi?
pairs.answer: Nihil sane, quod quidem aut tu audire velis aut ego pro certo dicere audeam.
pairs.derivation: Cicero greets Brutus and Atticus and asks if there is any news. Dropped the speech tags 'inquam' from the question and 'inquit Brutus' from the answer. Brutus's reply is one sentence answering 'nothing'; nothing cut after.

pairs.question: Quid tandem habuit liber iste, quod tibi aut novum aut tanto usui posset esse?
pairs.answer: Ille vero et nova mihi quidem multa et eam utilitatem quam requirebam, ut explicatis ordinibus temporum uno in conspectu omnia viderem.
pairs.derivation: Atticus asks what was new or useful in Atticus's book; Cicero answers it had much new and the usefulness he sought. Dropped 'inquam' from the answer; normalized the question's first-word capitalization. Ended the answer at the first full stop; what follows ('quae cum studiose tractare coepissem...') turns to how he handled it and a request to Atticus, so it was cut.

pairs.question: Quidnam id?
pairs.answer: Ut scribas aliquid; iam pridem enim conticuerunt tuae litterae.
pairs.derivation: Pomponius says he asks for what Cicero owes; Cicero asks 'what is it?'; the reply is 'that you write something.' Dropped 'inquam' from the question and 'inquit' from the answer. Kept through the first full stop (the semicolon-joined clause about his long silence); what follows ('nam ut illos de re publica libros edidisti...') elaborates, so it was cut.

pairs.question: Quidnam est id?
pairs.answer: Quod mihi nuper in Tusculano inchoavisti de oratoribus: quando esse coepissent, qui etiam et quales fuissent.
pairs.derivation: Atticus asks Cicero to set forth what they seek; Cicero asks 'what is it?'; Atticus answers it is the topic of orators begun at Tusculum. Dropped 'inquam' from the question and 'inquit' from the answer. Ended at the first full stop; what follows ('quem ego sermonem cum ad Brutum...') is narration, so it was cut.

pairs.question: Quonam istuc modo?
pairs.answer: Quia mihi et tu videris tantum iuris civilis scire voluisse quantum satis esset oratori et Servius eloquentiae tantum adsumpsisse, ut ius civile facile possit tueri; aetatesque vostrae ut illorum nihil aut non fere multum differunt.
pairs.derivation: Brutus claims a likeness between Cicero/Servius and Crassus/Scaevola; Cicero asks 'in what way?'; Brutus explains. Dropped 'inquam' from the question and 'inquit' from the answer. The answer is a single sentence ending at 'differunt'; nothing cut.

pairs.question: Ain tu? etiamne Q. Scaevolae Servium nostrum anteponis?
pairs.answer: Sic enim, Brute, existumo, iuris civilis magnum usum et apud Scaevolam et apud multos fuisse, artem in hoc uno.
pairs.derivation: Brutus asks whether Cicero really ranks Servius above Q. Scaevola; Cicero answers yes. Dropped 'inquit' from the question and 'inquam' from the answer (keeping the vocative 'Brute' as the speaker's own word). Ended the answer at the operative clause 'artem in hoc uno', normalizing the source semicolon to a full stop; what follows ('quod numquam effecisset ipsius iuris scientia...') elaborates, so it was cut.

pairs.question: Erit aut iam est iste quem exspectas?
pairs.derivation: Brutus asks whether the perfect orator Cicero awaits will yet appear or already exists; Cicero answers 'I do not know.' Dropped 'inquit M. Brutus' from the question and 'inquam' from the answer. The answer is the single word 'Nescio'; what follows ('sed est etiam L. Crassi...') moves on, so it was cut.

pairs.question: Quid tu, Brute? possesne, si te ut Curionem quondam contio reliquisset?
pairs.answer: Ego vero, ut me tibi indicem, in eis etiam causis, in quibus omnis res nobis cum iudicibus est, non cum populo, tamen si a corona relictus sim, non queam dicere.
pairs.derivation: Cicero asks whether Brutus could speak if abandoned by his audience as Curio once was; Brutus answers that he could not. Dropped 'inquit ille' from the answer. The answer is one sentence; nothing cut.

pairs.question: Quid igitur de illo iudicas quem saepe audisti?
pairs.answer: Quid censes nisi id quod habiturus es similem tui?
pairs.derivation: Cicero asks what Brutus judges of Caesar, whom he has often heard; Brutus answers that Caesar will turn out like Cicero. Dropped 'inquam' from the question and 'inquit' from the answer. Each is a single sentence; nothing cut.

pairs.question: Quidnam istuc est? aut quis est iste C. Rusius?
pairs.answer: Fuit accusator vetus, quo accusante C. Hirtilium Sisenna defendens dixit quaedam eius sputatilica esse crimina.
pairs.derivation: Brutus asks who C. Rusius is; Cicero answers he was an old accuser. Dropped 'inquit' from the question and 'Et ille:' plus 'inquit' from the answer. Ended at the first full stop ('crimina'); what follows ('tum C. Rusius...') is the anecdote that follows, so it was cut.

pairs.question: Quidnam est istuc? et quem ad modum distinguis?
pairs.answer: Hoc modo. cum honos sit praemium virtutis iudicio studioque civium delatum ad aliquem, qui eum sententiis, qui suffragiis adeptus est, is mihi et honestus et honoratus videtur.
pairs.derivation: Brutus asks what Cicero means and how he distinguishes (between honos and opes); Cicero answers 'this way' and defines the man truly honored. Dropped 'inquit' from the question and 'inquam' from the answer. Ended at the first full stop after the opening definition; what follows ('qui autem occasione aliqua...') develops the contrast, so it was cut.
